title: Cutdown is creeping up quickly — I currently have 55 players projected "inside" the 49ers' 53-man roster picture and may even add a couple more. How might SF fit all the players they need under the 53 limit? They have some tools: 🏈PUP list: 49ers can't add players to PUP, but those already there (i.e. Mykel, Guerendo) can stay there, not take up a 53 spot. Downside is they must miss at least 4 games 🏈Return-from-IR designations: 49ers can IR up to 2 players at the cutdown with a possibility to return after at least 4 games. These players also wouldn't take up a 53-man spot (we'll see where players like Toth and Kirk are at the cutdown) 🏈Release-and-re-sign trick: 49ers can cut a vet who wouldn't be exposed to waivers with the understanding that he'd be re-signed as soon as the next day when a roster spot opens with another player, who makes the 53-man roster, placed on IR. (In effect, a team can create more than 2 return-from-IR designations this way.) Key behind everything: A player must make the initial 53 in order to be return-eligible from IR unless he's one of the 2 designations, so — depending on the injury situation at the cutdown — there can be ways for a team to creatively "open" more 53-man roster space. The limiting factor is that only 8 players can be designated to return from IR in the regular season (2 more can come back if a team reaches the playoffs).

title: There is no astronomical $70 million average per year asking price from #Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud, per league sources, in his contract discussions with team. No deal is imminent at this time, per sources. Remains a possibility before season, but definitely not at that range and not close at this time. Barring new developments, this could stretch into next year. Both sides have time on their side. Stroud is secured through 2027 season on fifth-year club option. Plus, quarterback market is expected to rise significantly next year. A deal now could pale in comparison to potential value next year, especially if he has the kind of season team is hoping for. Should that happen, price obviously goes up. That's a good problem to have, not a deal-breaker at all. @KPRC2
